entries.title: Agent Skills and the Skills API (/v1/skills) are out of beta on the Claude API.
entries.summary: Requests no longer require the skills-2025-10-02 beta header, including Messages API requests that load Skills through the container parameter. Requests that still send the header continue to work unchanged.

entries.summary: The anthropic-beta: ce-user-management-2026-07-13 header is no longer required on group and custom-role requests; requests that still send it are accepted unchanged.

entries.title: You can now restrict which sites a Claude Managed Agents agent’s web_search and web_fetch tools can reach.
entries.summary: Set allowed_domains or blocked_domains on the tool’s entry in the agent_toolset_20260401 configs array; web_fetch also accepts max_content_tokens and web_search accepts user_location. Each configs entry is identified by its name and typed by an optional type, and requests that pass only name…

entries.title: Claude Managed Agents sessions that run in a self-hosted sandbox can now attach memory stores.
entries.summary: The Python, TypeScript, and Go SDK workers download each attached store into the sandbox at its mount_path and sync the agent’s changes back to the store.

entries.title: The session viewer in the Claude Console has been redesigned with a timeline minimap, a transcript grouped by model request, and an Inspector panel for session…
entries.summary: The session viewer in the Claude Console has been redesigned with a timeline minimap, a transcript grouped by model request, and an Inspector panel for session details and cost, raw events, per-tool statistics, mounted resources, and per-thread activity.

entries.title: Workbench is now playground in the Claude Console.
entries.summary: Playground supports every Messages API parameter and includes templates that demonstrate API features such as code execution and web search. It shows the full SDK request and the API response for each run, to help you understand the API and build with it. For more, see the Claude Help Center or try…

entries.title: The Compliance API now returns transcripts of Cowork and Claude Code sessions that run on your users’ machines, in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations.
entries.summary: GET /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/local lists sessions across your organization, GET /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/local/{session_id} retrieves one session’s metadata, and GET /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/local/{session_id}/messages returns its transcript, all with your existing Compliance Access Key…

entries.title: We’ve added the anthropic-workspace-id response header to the Claude API.
entries.summary: It carries the wrkspc_-prefixed ID of the workspace that the request’s API key or access token resolved to, including your organization’s Default Workspace.

entries.title: The introductory pricing for Claude Sonnet 5 ($2 / $10 USD per MTok) is now the standard price: the previously scheduled increase to $3 / $15 USD per MTok on…
entries.summary: The introductory pricing for Claude Sonnet 5 ($2 / $10 USD per MTok) is now the standard price: the previously scheduled increase to $3 / $15 USD per MTok on September 1, 2026, will not occur.

entries.title: You can now set a budget on a Claude Managed Agents session: a hard cap on the session’s spend, priced at public list rates.
entries.summary: A session that reaches its budget pauses with the budget_reached stop reason instead of starting new model requests; changing or removing the budget resumes it. Deployments accept the same budget and apply it to each session they start.

entries.title: You can now give a Claude Managed Agents session an advisor: a model at least as capable as the agent’s own that the session’s primary thread can consult…
entries.summary: You can now give a Claude Managed Agents session an advisor: a model at least as capable as the agent’s own that the session’s primary thread can consult mid-turn for strategic guidance. Configure it as a {"type": "advisor"} entry in the agent’s multiagent roster, naming the model to consult.

entries.title: You can now control where model inference runs for a Claude Managed Agents agent.
entries.summary: Set inference_geo inside the model object when you create the agent (see Pin the inference geo), or override it for a single session.

entries.title: Claude Managed Agents sessions can now load skills from a GitHub repository.
entries.summary: When a session mounts a repository, any skills in its root .claude/skills directory are discovered automatically at session start and available to the agent for that session.

entries.title: Skill and plugin security scanning (beta)
entries.summary: Enterprise plans can now turn on skill and plugin security scanning to automatically check third-party skills and plugins for malicious content when someone uploads or edits them.

entries.title: Inference hooks
entries.summary: are now in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations. Point Claude at your organization’s AI security server, and each governed prompt across claude.ai, Cowork, and Claude Code is held for the server’s allow or deny verdict before inference proceeds. entries.title: We’ve retired the Claude Opus 4.1 model (claude-opus-4-1-20250805).
entries.summary: All requests to this model on the Claude API will now return an error. We recommend upgrading to Claude Opus 5. Researchers can request ongoing access through the External Researcher Access Program.

entries.title: The Compliance API now returns transcripts of Cowork sessions started on claude.ai web or mobile, in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations.
entries.summary: GET /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/remote lists sessions and GET /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/remote/{session_id}/messages returns one session’s transcript, using your existing Compliance Access Key with the read:compliance_user_data scope.

Claude Opus 5 launch
entries.summary: We launched Claude Opus 5, a thoughtful and proactive model that comes close to the frontier intelligence of Claude Fable 5 at half the price.

entries.title: We’ve launched Claude Opus 5 (claude-opus-5), a step-change improvement over Claude Opus 4.8.
entries.summary: Claude Opus 5 supports a 1M token context window (both the default and the maximum), 128k max output tokens, and thinking on by default, at $5 / $25 USD per MTok, the same pricing as Claude Opus 4.8. It’s available on the Claude API, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude Models…

entries.summary: On Claude Opus 5, disabling thinking is allowed only at effort high or below: thinking: {"type": "disabled"} with effort xhigh or max returns a 400 error, a breaking change from Claude Opus 4.8.

entries.title: Effort is the primary control for steering Claude Opus 5: the model supports the full ladder (low, medium, high, xhigh, max), with max for capability-critical…
entries.summary: Effort is the primary control for steering Claude Opus 5: the model supports the full ladder (low, medium, high, xhigh, max), with max for capability-critical work.

entries.title: Mid-conversation tool changes are now in beta on Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 4.8, and Claude Opus 5: add or remove tools between turns of a…
entries.summary: Mid-conversation tool changes are now in beta on Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 4.8, and Claude Opus 5: add or remove tools between turns of a conversation while preserving the prompt cache. Include the mid-conversation-tool-changes-2026-07-01 beta header in your requests.

entries.title: The fallbacks parameter now supports a "default" mode, which applies Anthropic’s recommended fallback models by refusal category.
entries.summary: Server-side fallback is in beta, and the "default" mode requires the server-side-fallback-2026-07-01 beta header.

entries.title: We’ve removed fast mode for Claude Opus 4.7.
entries.summary: Requests to claude-opus-4-7 with speed: "fast" now return an error; unlike Claude Opus 4.6, they do not fall back to standard speed. Claude Opus 4.7 itself remains available at standard speed. To continue using fast mode, migrate to Claude Opus 5 or Claude Opus 4.8.

entries.title: You can now set an effort level on a Claude Managed Agents agent’s model configuration.
entries.summary: Pass effort inside the model object when you create the agent.

entries.title: Webhooks for Claude Managed Agents now cover the environment and memory store lifecycle: four environment.* event types and three memory_store.* event types.
entries.summary: You can react to environment and memory store lifecycle changes without polling.

entries.title: When creating a Claude Managed Agents session, you can now seed it with initial events.
entries.summary: Pass initial_events on POST /v1/sessions with up to 50 user.message and user.define_outcome events. A non-empty list starts the agent loop in the same call, so you don’t need a separate send-events request to start work.

entries.title: The version field is now optional when updating a Claude Managed Agents agent.
entries.summary: Supply it for optimistic concurrency (a mismatch returns a 409 error), or omit it to apply the update unconditionally.

entries.title: Claude Managed Agents session thread event streams now support event deltas.
entries.summary: GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/threads/{thread_id}/stream accepts the same event_deltas[] query parameter as the session-level stream, so you can preview a subagent’s text as the model generates it. A connection previews only the thread it’s reading.

entries.title: The legacy Workbench (platform.claude.com/workbench) in the Claude Console is being sunset with access ending on August 17, 2026.
entries.summary: Saved prompts, variables, and evals are not supported in the updated Workbench in the Console. You can export any data you want to keep from the banner and under your Organizational Settings. For more, see How do I use the Workbench? in the Claude Help Center.

entries.summary: Your monthly recap is a new feature at Settings > Reflect that shows you the topics you spent time on, your most active day and peak hour, and observations about how you work with Claude. entries.title: You can now set an expiration when you create an API key or an Admin API key in the Claude Console.
entries.summary: Choose a preset, a custom duration, or Never. For keys with a lifetime of at least 7 days, Anthropic emails the creator before expiration. Existing keys are unaffected. The Admin API reports each key’s expiration in the expires_at field.

entries.summary: Claude Cowork is now available on web and mobile in addition to desktop. entries.title: Claude Managed Agents session event streams now support event deltas.
entries.summary: Opt in with the event_deltas[] query parameter on GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/events/stream. The event_start and event_delta events preview an agent message’s text as it’s generated, before the complete agent.message event arrives.

entries.title: Listing sessions for Claude Managed Agents now supports backward pagination.
entries.summary: GET /v1/sessions returns a prev_page cursor alongside next_page; pass it as the page parameter to return to the previous page.

entries.title: When creating a Claude Managed Agents session, you can now override the agent’s configuration for that session.
entries.summary: Pass agent with type: "agent_with_overrides" to replace the model, system prompt, tools, MCP servers, or skills for a single session. The agent itself is unchanged.

entries.title: Claude Managed Agents vaults now support an injection_location setting on environment variable credentials (the Environment variable tab).
entries.summary: It controls whether the credential’s value is substituted, at egress, into the agent’s outbound request headers, the request body, or both.

entries.title: Webhooks for Claude Managed Agents now cover the agent, deployment, and deployment run lifecycle.
entries.summary: You can react to a newly published agent version, a paused deployment, or a failed scheduled run without polling.

entries.title: We’ve removed fast mode for Claude Opus 4.6.
entries.summary: Requests to claude-opus-4-6 with speed: "fast" no longer run at fast speed or premium pricing: they run at standard speed, are billed at standard rates, and do not return an error. The response’s usage.speed field reports the speed used. To continue using fast mode, migrate to Claude Opus 4.8.

entries.title: We’ve raised rate limits across the Claude API.
entries.summary: Claude Sonnet and Claude Haiku rate limits now match Claude Opus at every usage tier, and usage tiers have been consolidated into three: Start, Build, and Scale. entries.title: Enable Trusted Devices for Remote Control
entries.summary: Admins for Team and Enterprise plans can now require members to verify their device before viewing or steering local Claude Code sessions remotely.

entries.title: We’ve deprecated fast mode for Claude Opus 4.7, with removal on July 24, 2026.
entries.summary: After removal, requests to claude-opus-4-7 with speed: "fast" will return an error. Migrate to fast mode for Claude Opus 4.8.

entries.title: Delegate work to Claude in Slack with Claude Tag
entries.summary: Team and Enterprise plans can now tag Claude directly in Slack conversations and delegate tasks to it while they focus on other work.

entries.summary: All requests to these models on the Claude API will now return an error. We recommend upgrading to Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Claude Opus 4.8 respectively. Researchers can request ongoing access through the External Researcher Access Program.

entries.summary: When Claude writes a draft in chat or Claude Cowork (a report, a plan, a brief), it opens right beside your chat. Highlight the part you want changed, type the change, and Claude makes the edit right where you marked it. No switching apps, no re-describing paragraphs in chat.

entries.summary: The web search tool and web fetch tool now support web_search_20260318 and web_fetch_20260318, adding a response_inclusion parameter to drop consumed result blocks from the API response for agentic workflows. No beta header is required.

entries.summary: We extended the existing custom roles framework by adding admin permissions. Admin permissions give members access to specific administrative areas, like billing or privacy, without the need to make them Owners.

entries.summary: We added connector permissions to extend the existing custom roles framework and allow administrators to control which connectors, and which individual tools on those connectors, are available to each custom role.
